label: recent "2" or "n" input during the original/delimiter phase
explanation: Diffuse, token-driven candidate unit, active mostly in the original phase (82% of mass) and at the delimiter (8%); weak in the copy phase. The strongest driver is input 2 (33% rate, 6.6x lift, 27% of mass); next are n, then l, y, k, 1. It also fires one or two steps after those tokens (prev_tok 2/n about 4x lift), so it acts like a decaying trace of recently seen 2/n/y/1 tokens. Top activations happen at the last original token or at <DEL> right after a 2, in long sequences (L=8-9). Rate goes up with n_digits and with late original positions. The predicate (in_tok or prev_tok in {2, n}, before the copy phase) gets dev P 0.36 / R 0.47 / F1 0.41 / mass 0.57. Adding more tokens or longer lookback raises recall but lowers precision. Many activations come from spread-out token mixtures that no simple rule captures, so the explanation is incomplete.
